raw_case_text:
A 5-year-old girl was referred to the ear, nose and throat (ENT) clinic at a tertiary hospital with a 5-month history of right ear otalgia and foul smelling otorrhea. Symptoms had not resolved, despite two courses of oral co-amoxiclav received from a private general practitioner and local clinic, as well as a 6-week course of ciprofloxacin ear drops prescribed as three drops 8-hourly. The child was otherwise healthy with no previous history of significant illness. Screening for human immunodeficiency virus was negative. On clinical examination the patient was apyrexial and systemically well. No nasal obstruction or discharge was noted. Otoscopic examination revealed blood and pus in the right external auditory canal, from which a pus swab was sent from the outpatient department. The patient did not tolerate aural toilet in the clinic and was thus booked for examination under anaesthesia in theatre. Findings in theatre included an intact tympanic membrane on the right with prominent pus, debris, and a cotton-wool-like foreign body in the external auditory canal. The left ear had only wax visible. Both ears were cleaned in theatre, but no specimen sent to the laboratory. The child was discharged on ciprofloxacin ear drops for another 2 weeks, for a total treatment duration of 8 weeks of the fluroquinolone. A follow-up visit was booked at the ENT outpatient clinic in 6 weeks' time. On review the discharge was reported as resolved with no specific treatment of the Aspergillus niger cultured during the initial clinic visit. Grommets were inserted 2 months later.
Pus swabs are routinely inoculated onto 4% blood agar (anaerobic conditions), boiled blood agar (carbon dioxide conditions) and MacConkey media (aerobic conditions), incubated at 35  C for the isolation of bacteria and non-filamentous fungi. However, if a fungus is suspected and requested for culturing on the laboratory form, additional media will be inoculated to enhance the growth of a fungus. This includes Sabouraud Dextrose (SabDex) media with amikacin, incubated at 35  C and 25  C, as well as brain heart infusion agar incubated aerobically at 35  C. Furthermore, plates will be incubated for up to 3 weeks to monitor growth and up until 6 weeks if dimorphic fungi are suspected.
In this case Aspergillus niger was grown at 25  C and 35  C on SabDex media with amikacin from the pus swab taken from the outpatient department. Macroscopic appearance was of a flat surface with radial folds and a granular texture with characteristic black sporing heads covering white mycelium (Figure 1). The reverse of the fungus on the culture media plate had a cream colour. Microscopy of a lactophenol cotton blue stained impression showed thick walled conidiophores which had colourless stalks and were smooth with a round vesicle, phialides and metulae covering the entire surface. The conidia itself were round to oval, 5 microm - 10 microm and roughened (Figure 2).
Antifungal susceptibility testing is not offered for any topical agents (clotrimazole) in South Africa. In addition, no breakpoints are available for the interpretation of minimum inhibitory concentrations (MIC) of topical antifungal agents. It is likely that the delivery of an antifungal agent directly to the site of an infection will result in a very high concentration which is probably much higher than the MIC.
This article followed all ethical standards for carrying out research without direct contact with human or animal subjects.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 5-year-old girl presented with a 5-month history of right ear pain and foul-smelling bloody and purulent ear discharge.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Over the preceding 5 months, the child experienced persistent right otalgia and malodorous otorrhea that failed to resolve after two courses of oral amoxicillin-clavulanate and a 6-week course of topical ciprofloxacin ear drops (3 drops every 8 hours).
subjective.past_medical_history: Previously healthy, HIV-negative child with no significant past medical history.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for right otalgia and foul-smelling bloody/purulent otorrhea (5 months); negative for fever, nasal obstruction, or rhinorrhea.

objective.physical_examination: Afebrile and systemically well; initial outpatient otoscopy showed blood and pus filling the right external auditory canal (precluding clinic aural toilet). Examination under anesthesia in the operating theater revealed an intact right tympanic membrane with prominent pus, debris, and a retained cotton-wool-like foreign body in the right external auditory canal (left ear had only cerumen).
objective.advanced_workup: Culture of the outpatient right ear pus swab on Sabouraud dextrose agar with amikacin (at 25 C and 35 C) grew flat, radially folded colonies with black sporing heads over white mycelium and a cream reverse; lactophenol cotton blue microscopy confirmed Aspergillus niger (smooth, thick-walled colorless conidiophores, round vesicles covered circumferentially by biseriate metulae and phialides, and roughened 5-10 um round-to-oval conidia).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Secondary right Aspergillus niger otomycosis and chronic otitis externa associated with a retained cotton-wool-like foreign body in the external auditory canal, confirmed by examination under anesthesia and Sabouraud agar fungal culture and lactophenol cotton blue microscopy identifying A. niger. Treated with examination under anesthesia, complete removal of the foreign body and aural toilet, and an additional 2-week course of topical ciprofloxacin ear drops (without requiring topical antifungal therapy), achieving complete resolution of otorrhea at 6-week follow-up and subsequent tympanostomy tube (grommet) insertion 2 months later.
